findings.description: The while loop walking the __cause__ chain no longer tracks visited exceptions, so a cyclic __cause__ chain makes it loop forever when no cause matches the configured types.
findings.rationale: Trigger: the retried function raises an exception whose __cause__ chain forms a cycle (e.g. a.__cause__ = b and b.__cause__ = a, which Python permits when set manually) and none of the causes is an instance of exception_cause_types. The loop then keeps reassigning exc to __cause__ forever, since the removed seen-set was the only termination guard for that case. Impact: the retry predicate never returns, hanging the caller's thread instead of retrying or re-raising.
